description.narrative:
Assessment of Project Outcomes: The Project aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing of critical Li-B components in India, thereby reducing reliance on imports and supporting the expansion of the BESS and EV sectors. As Indias demand for Li-B cells continues to grow, the Project is expected to contribute to import substitution and position the country as a competitive exporter of battery materials. It will also promote greater local sourcing of raw materials, reaching up to 100% for select components such as PVDF (binder) and electrolytes. Beyond its economic impact, the Project will generate approximately 250 high-skilled direct jobs and create additional employment across the broader supply chain. It will further invest in workforce development to address skills gaps in this emerging sector, equipping local engineers and technicians with expertise in advanced chemical processes, materials science, and quality control. These efforts are expected to contribute meaningfully to Indias employment objectives and support its transition to a low-carbon economy.
Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: The Project aims to support the emergence of India as a competitive player in the global battery materials market by localizing the production of key Li-B components. In the context of a highly concentrated global supply chain, the Project will contribute to diversification efforts by establishing Indias first integrated battery materials facility, enhancing supply chain resilience and reducing production costs. Anchored in a rapidly growing domestic EV ecosystem and aligned with planned greenfield cell manufacturing investments, the Project is expected to catalyze broader development across the battery value chain. It will also facilitate deeper integration of India into global EV supply networks through exports, positioning both as strategic manufacturing and export hubs.

The proposed transaction involves an equity investment of up to INR 4.3 billion (approximately US$50 million equivalent) in GFCL EV Products Limited (GFCL EV or Company) in the form of Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS). IFC CCPS shall be converted to common shares at the time of Qualified Public Offering or other qualified liquidity event or equity financing round. GFCL EV is a newly established Indian manufacturer specializing in chemicals for Lithium-ion Battery (Li-B) cells used in electric vehicles (EV) and stationary battery energy storage systems (BESS). GFCL EV is focused on the manufacture of electrolytes, salts, binders and Cathode Active Material (CAM). These materials go into Li-B cells and most either contain, or are based on, fluorine chemistry. The Company was established as a wholly owned subsidiary of Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL or the Sponsor), an Indian chemical manufacturer with over 30 years of experience in fluorine chemistry. The Sponsor established GFCL EV with the aim of leveraging its manufacturing experience in fluorinated chemicals and backward integration into critical raw materials, to offer a cost-competitive alternative to global battery cell manufacturers looking to diversify their supply chain. The Company has began investing in a manufacturing facility in Gujarat, Maharashtra, close to the Sponsor's existing chemicals manufacturing facility. In addition, GFCL EV is also planning to establish a second facility in Oman in the future. The proposed IFC investment aims to support the Company's manufacturing facility in Gujarat, India (the Project), which is currently undergoing phased commissioning. The proposed IFC investment will promote domestic value-added manufacturing within India's Li-B supply chain, facilitate the creation of direct and indirect green jobs, and contribute to the availability of critical raw materials essential for transport electrification and BESS, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience and global competitiveness.
